decisive_items: duodenal diverticula, wall thickening with mesenteric edema approximately 25 cm beyond the ligament of Treitz, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy with luminal patency
10-day history of worsening, intermittent epigastric pain, distention, and constipation
response.rationale: CT shows duodenal diverticula with wall thickening, mesenteric edema, and lymphadenopathy, plus resolution on follow-up, strongly indicating diverticulitis. Other candidates lack specific imaging support or are contradicted by luminal patency and clinical course.

rejected.why: Luminal patency on CT contradicts small bowel obstruction.
No eosinophilic infiltration or peripheral eosinophilia; imaging points to diverticular inflammation.
Lacks chronic IBD features; no mucosal ulceration or chronic symptoms; family history alone insufficient.
Mesenteric panniculitis could explain edema/lymphadenopathy but diverticular wall thickening and resolution favor diverticulitis.
No mass, adenopathy pattern, or systemic symptoms typical of lymphoma; imaging more consistent with inflammation.
Gastroenteritis does not explain diverticula and mesenteric inflammatory changes on CT.
